attributes.title: RBO/SHIFT 2026
attributes.about:
The Royal Opera’s Associate Director Netia Jones curates a four-day festival exploring the shifting boundary between opera and technology. The focus for the first festival is the ever-growing world of artificial intelligence. What can AI offer creatives? And what can creatives offer the world in the age of AI?

Events for this inaugural festival include four EARLY SHIFT/LATE SHIFT sessions featuring performances and presentations from a diverse range of practitioners, the SHIFT EXCHANGE, a day of conversation with leading AI thinkers, and PLAY SHIFT, a relaxed day for all that encourages immersion and interaction. Alongside the four festival days, the Linbury Foyer will be open daily and free to the public and will feature exciting exhibitions and displays offering further interactive exploration.

Featured artists include legendary American experimental composer and improvisor George E. Lewis with soprano Juliet Fraser, Alexander Whitley Dance Company, vocal artist and AI innovator Harry Yeff (Reeps100) with soprano Patricia Auchterlonie, experimental composer Jennifer Walshe with vocal ensemble EXAUDI and AI sound artists Dadabots, composer Paola Prestini, AI sound artist and research scientist Yaboi Hanoi and transdisciplinary artist Stephanie Dinkins and many more.

Industry freelancers can access £20 tickets for SHIFT performances on Thursday and Saturday and £40 for SHIFT EXCHANGE. To receive the discount code, please email boxoffice@roh.org.uk
attributes.shortDescription: A new four-day festival connecting the worlds of opera and technology.

attributes.title: Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels Festival
attributes.about: For the fifth edition of its Festival, Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels – a programme launched in 2020 to strengthen the High Jewelry Maison’s commitment to the world of dance – returns to London. Following a successful run in 2022, the 2025 Festival will celebrate the wealth of international choreographic creation, from recent works to pieces from the repertory that have marked the history of contemporary dance.
attributes.shortDescription: Revel in the richness of choreographic creation.
attributes.carouselDescription: Revel in the richness of choreographic creation.

attributes.title: Festival of New Choreography
attributes.about:
The Festival of New Choreography is a series of performances, events and activities taking place across the House that embraces and champions new, diverse voices in choreography. The Festival, which will take place on the Main Stage, in the Linbury Theatre, Paul Hamlyn Hall and Clore Studio, is part of The Royal Ballet’s commitment to choreographic innovation and nurturing the future of the art form.

Four works created for The Royal Ballet are featured together on the Main Stage in New Works as part of the Festival of New Choreography. These works will introduce four exciting choreographers making their Main Stage debuts – Gemma Bond, Jessica Lang, Mthuthuzeli November and Royal Ballet First Artist Joshua Junker.

In the Linbury Theatre, The Royal Ballet presents an immersive work by Robert Binet that imagines the invisible forces of our universe in human form. This new work will be performed by dancers of The Royal Ballet.

Emerging choreographers come together in the Clore Studio to present short duets created for the Festival of New Choreography.

The Festival will also feature activity around the Royal Opera House, including Insight, Live at Lunch and Family Sunday events celebrating creativity and new thinking in dance.
attributes.shortDescription: The Festival of New Choreography is a series of performances and events that form part of The Royal Ballet’s commitment to embrace and champion new, diverse voices in choreography.

attributes.title: Rhythm in Resilience Festival
attributes.about:
For Black History Month, The Royal Ballet present Rhythm in Resilience, a new festival curated by Joseph Toonga, The Royal Ballet’s Choreographic Residency 23/24, which celebrates Black excellence within the Company over the years.  

The festival will highlight the stories of Black individuals through multiple platforms and conversations, while exploring future opportunities for diversifying The Royal Ballet and the wider ballet sector.

attributes.title: Engender Festival 2023
attributes.about:
This festival is centred around two new works by women, Woman at Point Zero and History of the Present.

The festival features an inspiring line-up of events. This includes conversations, gatherings and performances with leading creatives, writers, and both new and emerging voices from the world of opera and beyond. 

The festival welcomes audiences of all genders - come and join the conversation.

Please note, some events are exclusive to Mighty Network members only. To find out more about the Mighty Network and how to join, visit our Engender page.
attributes.shortDescription: The fourth annual Engender Festival celebrates more ground-breaking work from women and non-binary opera-makers, creatives and change-makers.
attributes.carouselDescription: The fourth annual Engender Festival celebrates more ground-breaking work from women and non-binary opera-makers, creatives and change-makers.

attributes.title: 8bit
attributes.about:
The Royal Opera embraces the digital stage in a series of eight newly-commissioned experimental experiences. 8bit – eight short ‘bits’ of digital opera – brings together some of the most innovative contemporary artists in five short films, two audio performances and a web browser experiment, all of which can be enjoyed from your own home. Expect well-loved repertory in ways you have never experienced before, as well as world premieres of new short works.

We welcome back Katie Mitchell, who leads a new film collaboration with Grant Gee and Anna Meredith, alongside new video pieces from Akhila Krishnan and Anna Morrissey, who collaborates with Royal Ballet dancers. Rakhi Singh, Patrick Eakin Young, André de Ridder, Katherine Manley, Elayce Ismail and Dumbworld make their Royal Opera House debuts.

The 8bit experience is available to watch from 30 April on the Royal Opera House's social media channels: YouTube, Facebook and Instagram.

Guidance

Please note that Heal You features needles and people receiving their COVID-19 vaccinations.

Please note that both FFAALL and Fatal Sytem Error feature flashing images.

previewImage.altText: An actor playing Tosca in Oliver Mears’ production of Tosca stands in a dramatic red gown against a marble-textured wall. Her hands are pressed above her head and her body angled towards it, while parts of the wall appear to be cracking around her. A strong diagonal shadow casts across the wall, adding depth and tension to the composition. The setting is abstract and theatrical, with cool-toned lighting contrasting against the flowing red fabric.

attributes.body: The Royal Ballet and Opera wants to open up the world of ballet and opera to many more people. Thanks to exceptional generosity and commitment of the Rothschild Foundation, we can share our thrilling performances that transport you and audiences across the globe to new worlds via Royal Ballet and Opera Stream.
